messages.subject: Simple array assignment question
parts:
Hey Guys,

From Chapter 5 of the manual I see an example for multiple indexing. However, I am actually wondering how to correctly do the part skipped in the ellipsis where we define c == (5,9,7).

I tried:

real C_t0[3];
C_t0 = (x_0, y_0, z_0);

However, that does not work. I get the error message 'PARSER EXPECTED: ")".' I've tried a few other variations that also do not work. Currently, I am doing it in the stupid way of

C_t0[1] = x_0;
 
and etc. and was wondering what the proper syntax to use was for the one-liner.

Thanks.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple array assignment question
parts:
Mitzi's going to add array, vector and matrix expression so
we'll be able to do that. But she's working on compound
declare and define first, so we'll be able to do this:

real a = 5;

Until then, you have to use brute force

C_t0[1] = x_0;
C_t0[2] = y_0;
C_t0[3] = z_0;

or write a function to create the array.

- Bob
